sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: POSITIVE TILT UPPER TROUGH OVER THE SWRN STATES WILL ADVANCE SLOWLY EAST THIS PERIOD WHILE A SERIES OF IMPULSES MOVE THROUGH THIS FEATURE. LEAD IMPULSE CURRENTLY OVER THE SRN AND CNTRL HIGH PLAINS WILL LIFT NWD THROUGH THE NRN PLAINS EARLY THURSDAY. A STRONGER UPPER JET NOW ROUNDING THE BASE OF THE TROUGH WILL EJECT NEWD THROUGH THE SRN PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON...REACHING THE CNTRL PLAINS BY EARLY EVENING. AT THE SURFACE A WARM FRONT WILL LIFT NWD ACROSS NERN TX...SERN OK AND THE LOWER MS VALLEY. A SURFACE LOW WILL DEVELOP NEWD ALONG THE FRONT IN ASSOCIATION WITH EJECTING UPPER JET. THIS FEATURE WILL REACH THE UPPER MS VALLEY LATE THURSDAY NIGHT. THE TRAILING COLD FRONT WILL ADVANCE SLOWLY EWD THROUGH THE CNTRL AND SRN PLAINS TODAY AND MID-LOWER MS VALLEY OVERNIGHT.

sections.title: SRN PLAINS THROUGH SERN KS...SWRN MO AND LOWER MS VALLEY
sections.text: RICH GULF MOISTURE WITH LOW 60S DEWPOINTS AS FAR NORTH AS ERN OK AND LOW 70S ACROSS ERN TX AND THE LOWER MS VALLEY WILL ADVECT NWD IN WAKE OF RETREATING WARM FRONT ALONG STRONG LOW LEVEL JET. MODEST MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND AREAS OF CLOUDS WILL LIKELY LIMIT MLCAPE TO AOB 1500 J/KG ACROSS MUCH OF THE WARM SECTOR...BUT MLCAPE COULD APPROACH 2000 J/KG WHERE LOW CLOUDS CAN MIX OUT. SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS...MOST OF WHICH SHOULD BE AT LEAST SLIGHTLY ELEVATED...MAY BE ONGOING EARLY THURSDAY MAINLY FROM NERN TX...ERN OK INTO THE LOWER MS VALLEY WITHIN ZONE OF STRONGER ISENTROPIC LIFT NORTH OF RETREATING WARM FRONT. UPPER FLOW WILL REMAIN MERIDIONAL EAST OF UPPER TROUGH AND MAY RESULT IN AT LEAST SLIGHT WARMING IN THE 850-500 MB LAYER ACROSS WARM SECTOR. THIS AND TENDENCY FOR DEEPER FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH EJECTING UPPER JET TO REMAIN POST FRONTAL RAISES CONCERNS THAT THE THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT COULD POTENTIALLY LIMIT THE ROBUSTNESS AND EXTENT OF SURFACE BASED THUNDERSTORMS IN WARM SECTOR. HOWEVER...VERTICAL SHEAR AND 0-1 KM HODOGRAPHS WILL REMAIN SUFFICIENT FOR A THREAT OF SUPERCELLS AND ISOLATED TORNADOES WITH ANY SURFACE BASED STORMS THAT DEVELOP. OTHER STORMS WILL LIKELY CONTINUE W

sections.title: ERN SRN PLAINS THROUGH SERN KS...SWRN MO AND LOWER MS VALLEY
sections.text: CONVECTIVE LINE AND COLD FRONT MOVING EWD THROUGH CENTRAL OK INTO NRN TX IS MOVING FASTER THAN FORCING IS SPREADING IN FROM THE WEST. HOWEVER...THE UPDRAFTS APPEAR TO HAVE SHIFTED TO THE FORWARD SIDE OF THE LINE AND THE MAGNITUDE OF THE SHEAR/ENVIRONMENTAL WINDS SHOULD SUPPORT A WIND THREAT WITH THIS LINE THROUGH THE MORNING AS IT PROGRESSES EWD...REFERENCE WW 780. ELSEWHERE...RICH GULF MOISTURE WILL COVER THE REGION AHEAD OF THE FRONT WITH DEWPOINTS RANGING FROM THE LOWER/MID 60S IN SRN MO/NRN AR TO THE LOWER/MID 70S ACROSS ERN TX AND THE LOWER MS VALLEY. WEAK MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND EXTENSIVE CLOUDS WILL LIMIT MLCAPE VALUES FROM 500 TO 1500 J/KG...BUT COULD APPROACH 2000 J/KG IN SERN TX WHERE WARMER TEMPERATURES AND HIGHER DEWPOINTS ARE ANTICIPATED. STRONG ENVIRONMENTAL WINDS WILL RESULT IN VERY STRONG LOW/DEEP LAYER SHEAR AND FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR SUPERCELLS AND LINES WITH BOW ECHOES. THE MAIN LIMITING FACTOR FOR SEVERE STORMS WILL BE THE WEAK FORCING IN THE WARM SECTOR. WARM ADVECTION WAS RESULTING IN MOSTLY SHALLOW CONVECTION TO FORM ACROSS PORTIONS OF CENTRAL/SERN TX THIS MORNING...AND IF THESE STORMS CAN BECOME ROOTED INTO THE BOUNDARY LAYER...THE MODERATE INSTABILITY

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: POTENT UPPER TROUGH AND ASSOCIATED DEEP SURFACE CYCLONE WILL CONTINUE TO TRACK NEWD ACROSS THE GREAT PLAINS TODAY AND TONIGHT. AS SURFACE LOW UNDERGOES OCCLUSION AND MOVES INTO THE UPPER MS VALLEY...TRAILING COLD FRONT WILL CONTINUE TO SPREAD EAST INTO MOIST AND UNSTABLE AIR MASS SITUATED ACROSS ERN OK AND ARKLATEX REGIONS THROUGH THIS EVENING.

sections.title: ERN OK ACROSS SRN MO AND THE ARKLATEX
sections.text: LARGE MERIDIONAL COMPONENT TO THE DEEP-LAYER FLOW EAST OF THE UNUSUALLY STRONG TROUGH ACROSS FOUR-CORNERS/NRN MEXICO WILL CONTRIBUTE TO RELATIVELY SLOW EWD PROGRESSION OF THE FRONTAL ZONE INTO THE WARM SECTOR TODAY. THIS SHOULD ALLOW FOR CONTINUED GRADUAL DIURNAL DESTABILIZATION GIVEN SOME BREAKS IN THE CLOUD COVER AND ONGOING SHOWERS/STORMS. REFER TO MCD 2156 FOR ADDITIONAL DETAILS REGARDING POSSIBLE TORNADO WATCH IN THE NEAR-TERM. MID-LEVEL JET STREAK OF 110-120KT APPEARS TO BE ROUNDING THE BASE OF THE LARGE SCALE TROUGH OVER NRN MEXICO PER WV IMAGERY AND MORNING RAOBS FROM SWRN STATES AND MEXICO. AS THE UPPER TROUGH BEGINS TO LIFT NEWD FROM THE ROCKIES/SRN HIGH PLAINS THROUGH THIS AFTERNOON...MODEL GUIDANCE CONTINUES TO INDICATE THAT STRONGEST 500MB HEIGHT FALLS /GREATER THAN 60M PER 12H/ WILL OCCUR TO THE NORTH OF GREATEST WARM SECTOR DESTABILIZATION. THIS SCENARIO DOES INTRODUCE SOME UNCERTAINTY WITH REGARD TO SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT AND EVOLUTION. LATEST INDICATIONS ARE THAT EVEN WEAK HEIGHT FALLS AND DPVA ACCOMPANYING THE EWD MOVEMENT OF THE UPPER TROUGH WILL CONTRIBUTE TO ENHANCED ASCENT ALONG THE ADVANCING COLD FRONT FROM SERN OK ACROSS THE ARKLATEX INTO THE EVENING HOURS

sections.title: EASTERN TX/ARKLATEX VICINITY/OZARKS
sections.text: MULTIPLE/NEAR COLD FRONTAL BROKEN BANDS OF CONVECTION WILL CONTINUE TO STEADILY DEVELOP EAST-NORTHEASTWARD THROUGH THE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING ACROSS THE REMAINDER OF FAR EASTERN OK/NORTHEAST TX INTO WESTERN AR...PERHAPS AIDED BY AN EASTWARD PROGRESSING BAND OF IMPLIED LARGE SCALE ASCENT PER LATEST WATER VAPOR IMAGERY. WITH 18Z OBSERVED RAOBS FROM SHREVEPORT/LAKE CHARLES REFLECTING A VERY MOIST/WEAKLY CAPPED WARM SECTOR BOUNDARY LAYER...OTHER MORE DISCRETE/POTENTIALLY ROTATING STORMS WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP INTO THE EVENING ACROSS THE REMAINDER OF THE ARKLATEX/SABINE RIVER VICINITY ALONG/SOUTH OF A NORTHWARD RETREATING WARM FRONT...WHICH GENERALLY ANGLES NW-SE FROM SOUTHWEST AR INTO CENTRAL MS AS OF 20Z. WITH REGIONAL WSR-88D VWP DATA INDICATIVE OF 200-350 MS/S2 OF 0-1 KM OF SRH...AMPLE LOW LEVEL SRH/HIGH MOISTURE CONTENT AIRMASS WILL SUPPORT POTENTIAL FOR ROTATING STORMS/POSSIBLE TORNADOES ESPECIALLY WITH QUASI-DISCRETE STORMS ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR...EVEN WITH AN INCREASINGLY MERIDIONAL LARGE SCALE REGIME. STORM MERGERS/MERIDIONAL NATURE OF THE FORCING SHOULD ULTIMATELY LEAD TO QLCS DEVELOPMENT LATER TONIGHT...WITH SOME DAMAGING WIND/ISOLATED TORNADO RISK CONTINUING. FARTHER NOR

sections.title: ERN TX THROUGH LOWER MS VALLEY
sections.text: EARLY THIS EVENING A COLD FRONT EXTENDS FROM A SURFACE LOW IN NERN KS SWD THROUGH EXTREME WRN AR...ERN AND SRN TX. A WARM FRONT STRETCHES FROM NRN FL NWWD THROUGH NRN MS...CNTRL AND EXTREME WRN AR WHERE IT INTERSECTS THE COLD FRONT. THE COLD FRONT WILL ADVANCE EAST OVERNIGHT AS THE SURFACE LOW LIFTS TOWARD THE UPPER MS VALLEY IN ASSOCIATION WITH EJECTING 100+ KT UPPER JET. A VERY MOIST WARM SECTOR HAS ADVECTED WELL INLAND WITH LOW-MID 70 F DEWPOINTS FROM ERN TX THROUGH THE LOWER MS VALLEY INCLUDING VALUES AROUND 70 F AS FAR NORTH AS CNTRL AR. DESPITE ABUNDANT LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE...RELATIVELY WARM AIR ALOFT /-6 TO -8 C AT 500 MB/ AND 700-500 MB LAPSE RATES AOB 6.5 C/KM ARE LIMITING MLCAPE TO GENERALLY AOB 1500 J/KG ALONG WITH MODEST NORMALIZED CAPE. THE MARGINAL THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT HAS BEEN THE PRIMARY LIMITING FACTOR FOR A MORE WIDESPREAD SEVERE EVENT. THE COLD FRONT IS IN THE PROCESS OF MERGING WITH THE MORE DISCRETE CONVECTION THAT DEVELOPED IN THE WARM SECTOR. AS THIS OCCURS A GRADUAL INCREASE IN LINEAR MODES WILL LIKELY OCCUR THIS EVENING. HOWEVER...STORMS WILL REMAIN EMBEDDED WITHIN A STRONG DEEP LAYER FLOW WITH LARGE LOW LEVEL HODOGRAPHS AND BULK SHEAR MORE THAN ADEQUATE

sections.title: S TX
sections.text: GREATER INSTABILITY AND LAPSE RATES EXIST OVER S TX WITH 3000-3500 J/KG MLCAPE ON 00Z OBSERVED CRP AND BRO RAOBS. CONVECTION WILL LIKELY CONTINUE TO STRUGGLE OVER S TX DUE TO A STRONGER CAPPING INVERSION PRESENT BETWEEN 850-700 MB. STORMS MAY EVENTUALLY DEVELOP LATER THIS EVENING ALONG SEWD ADVANCING BAROCLINIC ZONE...BUT GIVEN THE NATURE OF THE CAP...THE MORE ROBUST UPDRAFTS WILL PROBABLY BE POST FRONTAL WHERE DEEPER LIFT MAY EXIST TO OVERCOME THE INVERSION. ..DIAL.. 10/30/2009
